newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Rain, disease slash 1997 Zimbabwe maize crop.
newsitem.headline: Rain, disease slash 1997 Zimbabwe maize crop.

text.p: Waterlogging and disease slashed Zimbabwe's staple maize crop this year to less than 2.1 million tonnes from an expected bumper harvest of 2.8 million, a top industry official said on Wednesday.
Zimbabwe was looking to export 500,000 tonnes of maize this year but Zimbabwe Cereal Producers' Association chief executive Peter Wells said this had now been revised down to 200,000 tonnes.
"Preliminary forecasts show an official maize crop of just under 2.1 million tonnes," Wells told Reuters.
"There was potential for a bumper crop of 2.8 million tonnes but we have had a lot of waterlogging and a lot of disease so the potential yield dropped quite a bit," he said.

Last year, Zimbabwe produced 2.6 million tonnes of maize and was on course to surpass that this year before excessive rains and grey leaf disease reduced yields. Industry officials however said the harvest would be enough to meet domestic consumption with some leftover for export.
"There will be some prospects for exports although the tonnages will be very much lower than expected," Wells said.
Zimbabwe exports surplus maize to other southern African countries such as Zambia, Mozambique, Malawi and sometimes South Africa.
On recent press reports that South African farmers were trying to block a consignment of local maize, Wells said the South Africans wrongly believed the Zimbabwean crop was subsidised.

"Although there are controls on maize imports and exports, there's no subsidy on our crop. But because the South Africans have changed to a free market situation literally overnight they are feeling a bit exposed," he said.

He declined further comment, referring questions to the state-owned Grain Marketing Board (GMB) which controls maize imports and exports. GMB officials were unavailable for comment. --Harare Newsroom +263-4 72 52 27/8/9
